ref_file_title: Adl78 - Two theorems on random polynomial time
note: Verified independently via web search: ACM DL / IEEE record for the 19th FOCS (1978), pp. 75-83, DOI 10.1109/SFCS.1978.37. Adleman's theorem. The paper proves the one-sided-error (RP) case; the BPP form is universally credited to it (e.g. Arora-Barak Thm 7.14) and first appears in BG81. doi.org is egress-blocked from this environment; the DOI was cross-checked against the ACM DL listing surfaced by search.

ref_file_title: BB04 - Efficient Selective-ID Secure Identity Based Encryption Without Random Oracles
note: Introduces the selective-ID model and the complexity-leveraging observation that a selective-ID secure IBE with N identities is fully secure with loss N. eprint 2004/172; cryptobib_key: EC:BonBoy04b. The explicit theorem is stated in the Journal of Cryptology version, 'Efficient Selective Identity-Based Encryption Without Random Oracles', J. Cryptology 24(4):659-693, 2011, doi:10.1007/s00145-010-9078-6 (cryptobib JC:BonBoy11). Boneh–Boyen have two other 2004 papers (CRYPTO 2004 'Secure Identity Based Encryption Without Random Oracles'; EUROCRYPT 2004 'Short Signatures Without Random Oracles'); either would need a suffixed key.

ref_file_title: BB15 - On Basing Size-Verifiable One-Way Functions on NP-Hardness
note: cryptobib TCC:BogBrz15, pp. 1-6, DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-46494-6_1; also ECCC TR14-108. Abstract (via search snippet): if the hardness of inverting a size-verifiable one-way function can be based on NP-hardness via a general (adaptive) reduction, then NP subset-of coAM; this claim was made by AGGM06 and later retracted. Recovers, for size-verifiable f, the adaptive case AGGM06 withdrew.

ref_file_title: BBS86 - A Simple Unpredictable Pseudo-Random Number Generator
authors: Lenore Blum, Manuel Blum, Michael Shub
note: cryptobib_key: BluBluShu86 (verified in vendor/cryptobib). DOI 10.1137/0215025. Introduces the $x^2 \bmod N$ generator over Blum integers and proves it unpredictable under the quadratic residuosity assumption. Crypto 1982 precursor with a different title: 'Comparison of Two Pseudo-Random Number Generators' (C:BluBluShu82).

ref_file_title: BCCGP16 - Efficient Zero-Knowledge Arguments for Arithmetic Circuits in the Discrete Log Setting
authors: Jonathan Bootle, Andrea Cerulli, Pyrros Chaidos, Jens Groth, Christophe Petit
note: Introduces the recursive inner-product argument and a protocol to commit to a polynomial and later reveal its evaluation at an arbitrary point verifiably, sound under DLOG in prime-order groups. EUROCRYPT 2016, LNCS 9666, pp. 327-357, DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-49896-5_12. Verified in vendor/cryptobib: cryptobib_key EC:BCCGP16.

ref_file_title: BCCT13 - Recursive Composition and Bootstrapping for SNARKs and Proof-Carrying Data
authors: Nir Bitansky, Ran Canetti, Alessandro Chiesa, Eran Tromer
note: eprint 2012/095. Verified against vendor/cryptobib STOC:BCCT13 (DOI 10.1145/2488608.2488623) and web-search snippets of the abstract: any SNARK yields PCD for constant-depth distributed computations; a depth-reduction turns constant-depth PCD into PCD over paths of fixed polynomial length (IVC); preprocessing SNARKs bootstrap to fully succinct ones. cryptobib_key: STOC:BCCT13.
